The purpose of this procedure is to
provide detailed safe method for transmission lines maintenance staff to
minimize the possibility of error causing personal injury or damage to equipment
for Lowering 500KV Middle and Side Bundles to the Ground for Repair.

EEHC_TL engineers in head office and
zones using their background field experience and EEHC documentation to create
this procedure.

items:
A worker must climb up the tower 1 to ensure isolation and apply earthings
 on the three phases of towers no.1&3 Fig.1, given that work will be
 carried out on tower no. 2. The middle and side phases of tower no.2 must be
 earthed directly before reaching the ground to be discharged.

Two climbing technicians must climb the tower up to the conductor where
 the work is taking place and install one hand line at the cross arm angle
 next to the middle phase and another at the angle next to the side phase.
 Two 6 ton Russian block must also be raised one of which is fixed above the
 middle phase plate, while the other must be fixed above that of the side
 phase. Another snatch block must be attached at the tower leg.

The bulldozer winch cable (80 m in length, 16 mm in diameter) must be
 raised and attached to the L joint of the middle phase through the tower leg
 snatch block and the middle phase Russian block.

Using the bulldozer winch cable, the insulator string must be slackened
 then the L joint pin must be released and both the strings and the conductor
 lowered to the ground , given that they must be earthed immediately before
 they reach the ground as previously mentioned. Then untie the bulldozer
 winch cable.

As for the side phase, the bulldozer winch cable must be attached to the
 side phase L joint through the tower leg snatch block, which must be
 conveniently placed at the side phase Russian block.

The side phase is similarly lowered and earthed before reaching the
 ground.

Two grips must be installed on the worn out conductor at a distance of 30
 m from the tower, after the spacers of whole three spacers group at either
 side of the insulator strings must also be released.

One of the grips must be attached to the front side of the bulldozer by a
 steel wire ,while the other grip must be attached to the wire at the back of
 the bulldozer as illustrated in the Fig.(2).

The bulldozer is operated in order to apply tension on both wires
 slackening the part of the conductor between both grips. The worn out
 conductor is then cut at a distance of at least 25m at either side from the
 tower center.

The ends of the old conductors where the cutting took place must be
 entirely cleaned , and the new conductor is brought given that the
 measurement must be accurately performed.

Apply bandage at both terminals of the conductor
 (the terminal of the old
 conductor as well as the new one) at a distance of 5 mm from each side as
 shown in Figure (4-a).

The conductor is then inserted in the middle aluminum joint as shown in
 Figure (4-b).

Apply another bandage at a distance of 145 mm from conductor end at the
 both side as shown in Fig. (4-c). Peel the aluminum strands off the steel
 core for a distance of 145mm from the bandage at both ends

Insert both ends of the conductor into the steel joint till they touch at
 exactly the midpoint of the steel joint Fig.(5 a).

Press at the midpoint of the joint (i.e. at the point of contact of the
 conductor ends), using a press with the suitable dies. Press on at both ends
 of the conductor till the end of the joint, given that each two presses must
 overlap by 25% Fig.(5 - b).
File the steel joint then apply conductive grease on it.

Slide the aluminum joint on the steel one, till the latter becomes at the
 middle of the aluminum joint.

Replace the steel press dies by aluminum ones, then press once more
 starting at both ends of the steel joints till the end of the aluminum
 joint.

Install another joint at the other end of the conductor following the same
 procedures mentioned above. The conductor is thus entirely repaired.

The conductor and the grips must then be released, the bulldozer moved
 away and the conductor re-connected to the insulators. All spacers must then
 be re-fixed and local earthings disconnected.

The work location must be cleared of all workers and equipment, and the
 side phase must then be raised and installed once more in its initial
 position.
Earthing of the middle phase must also be disconnected.

The tower must be cleared of all equipment and the local earthings of the
 other towers disconnected.

The work permit must be completed and the control informed that that
 circuit is ready for re-connection.
